reasoning_content:
The app is a static site. Elasticsearch is a separate service (a prerequisite) but not part of the software being installed. The guide says Elasticsearch Service is a prerequisite but ES is external infrastructure, not part of the app. The app itself is static files served over web server. The installation task is serving the files.

Let me verify page loads by curl content. Also check that index.html references resolve (403 on directory listing is normal - directory index disabled, that's fine since try_files $uri $uri/ =404; actually 403 means autoindex off; fine).

Let me verify the i18n JSON fetch works and that the app can initialize. Let me do a more behavioral test - actually rendering the JS. No browser available. Let me at least verify with node if possible? node not installed.

Let me check whether the 13 missing refs matter. Those are inside vendored packages (spec/test files) and examples referencing relative root paths. Examples like examples/fcd/csvParseFcd.html references 'src/css/dataExplorer.css' relative — but guide says HTML pages in examples folder are functional when copied to document root. They're not expected to work in-place. Actually the guide says "all the HTML pages on toplevel or in one of the folders in subfolder examples can be copied to the document root folder and are functional there". So in-place they may not work; that's expected. So those missing refs aren't failures.

Let me verify the app's runtime by fetching i18n files and config. Already 200 on config. Check i18n en.json.

Also let me confirm there's no index.php needed. The app needs php only if browser has no access to ES. Not required.

Let me check logs for errors when serving. And run a quick headless check maybe using python to simulate? Not much value.

Let me verify key js module fetch of the deeper imported modules via HTTP (the ones imported recursively). Let's just curl a few.

Actually I already resolved relative imports exist on disk, and nginx serves src files with 200. Good.

Let me test the i18n and a couple of src modules over HTTP.

The main question: Is this "success"? The software is a static web app served by nginx. It's operational to the extent it can be without Elasticsearch. The guide explicitly lists Elasticsearch as a prerequisite, external to the app. The installation summary notes no ES installed, and live querying requires ES. Since ES is a prerequisite that a validation might consider necessary... But the software itself (frontend) is served correctly.

Hmm. The definitions: "complete and operational according to the supplied guide." The guide says prerequisites include Elasticsearch Service. But the installation attempt only set up the webserver/files. Is the task to validate the app installation? I think we should assess whether the static app is served and functional. The frontend loads and initializes; it would show the UI. Without ES, it can't query data, but ES is an external service not part of the repo/installation.

Let me do a deeper behavioral test. Maybe I can use python to check the JS initializes? Hard without browser. Could install nothing (prohibited). Node not present.

I'll gather HTTP evidence for all the app's direct resources and the config/i18n, which is solid. Let me also try to fetch the page and confirm title etc.

Let me get i18n en.json status and content snippet.

action.command: cd /workspace && for f in i18n/en.json i18n/de.json src/js/models/ElasticsearchModel.js src/js/helpers/I18nTranslator.js src/js/helpers/ConfigHelper.js src/js/configurators/GenericProfilingConfigurator.js logo.png; do code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8080/$f); echo "$code  $f"; done; echo "--- i18n content head ---"; curl -s http://localhost:8080/i18n/en.json | head -c 200; echo; echo "--- nginx error log tail ---"; tail -5 /var/log/nginx/error.log 2>/dev/null

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace && for f in i18n/en.json i18n/de.json src/js/models/ElasticsearchModel.js src/js/helpers/I18nTranslator.js src/js/helpers/ConfigHelper.js src/js/configurators/GenericProfilingConfigurator.js logo.png; do code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\" http://localhost:8080/$f); echo \"$code  $f\"; done; echo \"--- i18n content head ---\"; curl -s http://localhost:8080/i18n/en.json | head -c 200; echo; echo \"--- nginx error log tail ---\"; tail -5 /var/log/nginx/error.log 2>/dev/null", "summary": "Verify i18n, modules, logo served"}
